*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/generate_options.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+values = duckdb.connect().execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::BIGINT AS pedestrians_killed
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """
+).df()
+
+expected_years = list(range(2013, 2026))
+assert values["year"].tolist() == expected_years
+values["year"] = values["year"].astype(int)
+values["pedestrians_killed"] = values["pedestrians_killed"].astype(int)
+
+answer = "Annual pedestrian deaths were " + "; ".join(
+    f"{row.year}: {row.pedestrians_killed}"
+    for row in values.itertuples(index=False)
+) + "."
+
+for option_id, chart_type in ((1, "bar"), (2, "line")):
+    values.to_csv(OUT / f"values_{option_id}.csv", index=False)
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5), constrained_layout=True)
+    years = values["year"]
+    deaths = values["pedestrians_killed"]
+    if chart_type == "bar":
+        bars = ax.bar(years, deaths, color="#276FBF", width=0.72)
+        ax.bar_label(bars, padding=3, fontsize=8)
+    else:
+        ax.plot(years, deaths, color="#276FBF", marker="o", linewidth=2)
+        for year, count in zip(years, deaths):
+            ax.annotate(str(count), (year, count), xytext=(0, 7),
+                        textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8)
+    ax.set_title("Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes, 2013–2025")
+    ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+    ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrians killed (people)")
+    ax.set_xticks(expected_years)
+    ax.set_ylim(0, max(deaths) * 1.18)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    fig.savefig(OUT / f"option_{option_id}.png", dpi=180)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed",
+            "denominator": "None; absolute count of pedestrian fatalities",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year of crash_date (2013–2025)",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "Bars make it easy to compare the absolute fatality count across individual calendar years.",
+            "probability": 0.6,
+            "answer": answer,
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers how many pedestrians were killed in each requested year, using the sum of the crash-level pedestrian-fatality counts. Comparing annual totals with bars is defensible because the question asks for yearly counts rather than rates. It does not show the number of pedestrians exposed to traffic or explain causes of changes.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed",
+            "denominator": "None; absolute count of pedestrian fatalities",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year of crash_date (2013–2025)",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "A line chart emphasizes the year-to-year trajectory while preserving the requested annual counts.",
+            "probability": 0.4,
+            "answer": answer,
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers the annual-count question and highlights how the counts move over time from 2013 through 2025. A line is defensible for ordered yearly observations when the temporal pattern is of interest. It does not show exposure-adjusted risk or explain why the count changes.",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+
+with (OUT / "options.json").open("w") as f:
+    json.dump(options, f, indent=2)
+    f.write("\n")
*** End Patch
